newsitem.title: UK: Angry overseas pensioners attack UK government.
newsitem.headline: Angry overseas pensioners attack UK government.

text.p: Aggrieved representatives of nearly half a million British retirees living abroad denounced the government on Wednesday for refusing to raise their state pensions in line with inflation.

Some 330,000 overseas pensioners, including those in the European Union and the United States, get cost-of-living rises, but the remaining 430,000 do not -- their pensions are frozen at the rate in force on the date they retired or left Britain.

Representatives of these "frozen" pensioners -- most of whom live in Australia, Canada, New Zealand and South Africa -- told parliament's Social Security committee that Britain had a moral duty to end what they said was indefensible discrimination.
"Quite frankly, pensioners out there are mad," Richard Corner, secretary-general of the World Alliance of British Expatriate Pensioners, told the committee.

"They are particularly mad that the British government of all governments in the world -- the home of parliament -- can behave in this despicable manner and discriminate against people who pay the same contributons but live in different lands. It is quite utterly ridiculous," Corner said.
He said Britain was the only developed country to discriminate in this way.

In a note to the committee, the Department of Social Security said successive governments had considered it would be unfair to fund cost-of-living increases for pensioners who have chosen to retire abroad. Only those in countries that have signed reciprocal agreements with Britain receive the increases.
The ministry said it would cost 255 million pounds ($421.2 million) a year to unfreeze the affected pensions and admitted the government was simply not prepared to find the money.

"Agreeing to incur additional expenditure on pensions paid overseas would be incompatible with the government's policy of containing the long-term cost of the social security system to ensure that it remains affordable," the ministry said.
Douglas Ross, president of the Canadian Alliance of British Pensioners, said many retired expatriates were suffering extreme hardship because of the payments freeze.
"They feel the British government has completely let them down on this issue," Ross said. ($1=.6054 Pound)
